corrections.form_value: Thirty Prolific workers were recruited through separate study postings for three conditions (AI-Prohibited, AI-Optional, AI-Mandatory) and answered five open-ended questions about a business ethics dilemma (whether a company should disclose a product defect). One AI-Mandatory participant was dropped for not using AI, leaving 29 (10, 10, 9). Three blind coders counted distinct perspective categories (Perspective Diversity Index) and counterargument categories (Counterargument Diversity Score) in each response; the paper does not say that assignment to conditions was random.

Criterion 3 unclear: the outcomes are blind-coded counts of perspective and counterargument categories in each person's answer, but the task is ethical reasoning about a business dilemma, not a creative or ideation task as the codebook defines it. confirmed: The complete markdown and all 30 PDF pages were read, including Appendices A-D. The title and author Byeongmu Choi match the form (PDF p. 1); no manuscript date or arXiv version number is printed. PDF metadata gives creation date 2026-07-13, which is not a posting date; arXiv provenance comes from retrieval.json, and the catalog first-posted date is not established by this PDF.

One between-subjects pilot is reported, with separate recruitment into AI-Prohibited, AI-Optional, and AI-Mandatory conditions; quasi_people describes the reported separate-group comparison, subject to the unreported allocation mechanism (PDF p. 5, Section 2.1). No additional randomized people study appears in the appendices (PDF pp. 18-30).

Thirty people were recruited; one AI-Mandatory participant was excluded for nonuse without the required evidence, leaving 29 analyzed: 10 Prohibited, 10 Optional, 9 Mandatory. These are people, not texts or ratings; randomized counts are unreported and appropriately null. Fewer than 50 were analyzed, so criterion 2 is not met and core='no' is correct (PDF p. 5, Section 2.2; p. 9, Section 3.2).

Prolific recruitment criteria were approval rate at least 95% and 50 to 5,000 previous submissions, from the listed English-speaking countries; age, gender, and occupation were not collected. The advertised duration was approximately 12 minutes and payment was GBP 3 (PDF p. 5, Section 2.2).

The task was one business-ethics dilemma with five open-ended questions about actions, stakeholders, counterarguments, risks, and alternative perspectives. It did not directly rate novelty, usefulness, or overall creativity, supporting the retained task-scope uncertainty (PDF pp. 6-7, Section 2.3; pp. 28-29, Appendices C-D).

AI was prohibited, optional, or required as described; ChatGPT, Claude, and Gemini are examples rather than a specified model/version. Optional use was six reporting no AI, one discussion-partner user, and three nonresponses; the nine retained Mandatory participants supplied evidence. The first exchange was required and fuller conversation submission optional (PDF pp. 7-9, Sections 2.4 and 3.2; pp. 26-27 and 29-30, Appendices B and D).

Three independent condition-blind coders counted distinct categories within each participant's written response. The recorded CDS and PDI category lists match Appendix A; these measure within-person flexibility rather than similarity across different people's outputs (PDF p. 8, Section 2.5; pp. 18-25, Appendix A; creativity-codebook.md, Section 6).
ICC(2,k) is 0.868 for CDS and 0.817 for PDI, exactly as recorded (PDF pp. 8-9, Section 3.1 and Table 1).

All PDI reported numbers match: Prohibited n=10, mean 0.87, SD 0.61; Optional n=10, mean 0.87, SD 0.67; Mandatory n=9, mean 2.30, SD 1.72; F(2,26)=5.31, p=.012, eta squared=.290; Cohen's d=1.13 for Mandatory versus Prohibited and 1.12 versus Optional (PDF p. 10, Table 3 and Section 3.4).

All CDS reported numbers match: Prohibited n=10, mean 1.47, SD 1.34; Optional n=10, mean 1.53, SD 0.91; Mandatory n=9, mean 1.96, SD 1.30; F(2,26)=0.48, p=.626, eta squared=.035 (PDF p. 9, Table 2 and Section 3.3).

The one-line finding reproduces the participant count, group means, test statistics, p values, effect size, and association direction correctly; PDI differs across conditions and CDS does not reach statistical significance (PDF pp. 9-10, Tables 2-3 and Sections 3.3-3.4).

This is an original pilot, not a synthesis, so no pooled estimates or study counts apply. Appendices A-D contain coding rules, participant instructions, the scenario, and questions without additional sample/effect statistics; anonymized data and coding materials are available upon reasonable request, with no public data/code URL stated (PDF p. 16, Data Availability Statement; pp. 18-30).
summary: The PDF confirms 30 recruits, 29 analyzed participants, and every reported outcome statistic, but does not document randomized assignment. Corrections concern unsupported recruitment detail, randomization certainty and triage attribution, the quasi_people-to-observational context mapping, and both outcomes' explicitly stated primary status.
